matches.quote: Define the "dynamic velocity" in Fig. 5 (peak or pulse-averaged).
Sublattice A contains FeCoB/CoFeB (Fig. 1a), so the Co L3 signal includes an opposite-sign contribution from sublattice A in addition to the CoB sublattice B.
Any elastic restoring force from a local pinning well... is therefore absorbed into a*, b*. The result is then a lumped effective potential, not the intrinsic skyrmion–skyrmion interaction
Discuss the origin of the difference (stack, dense array compared with isolated skyrmions, residual pinning... The "viscous flow" interpretation also needs the v(J) intercept and threshold.
Show that the exponential form is preferred over alternatives such as a K1-type decay or a power law.
fitting v(t) to the drive convolved with the instrument response with a free delay
The I/M/L/R classification from a single displacement map (Fig. 2a) should be given with its thresholds.
The simulation parameters (... interlayer exchange...) are not given in the main text. It is unclear whether they were measured independently... Give the parameters and their provenance.
Estimate the temperature rise, for example from the time-resolved device resistance during the pulse or from a thermal simulation. State the temperature during the 1.2×10^12 A/m² runs.
Explain why τ_relax for the same class differs by up to a factor of 2.5 between polarities (L: 9.6 vs 3.9 ns; R: 7.4 vs 18.9 ns, Table 1).
The tracked core position of a deforming skyrmion also relaxes through shape (breathing/elongation) relaxation, which a centre-to-centre force cannot represent.

notes: C5 and C16 are marked 'partly' because the review challenges the empirical exponential and pairwise centre-to-centre rigid-particle assumptions by requesting comparisons with K1/power-law forms, static two-skyrmion micromagnetic energies, and shape-deformation/multi-region checks rather than an analytical derivation from microscopic interactions. C15 is 'partly' because the review asks for the provenance of the interlayer exchange parameter and a quantitative bound on the interlayer lag/effective mass relative to Ref. 43.
